newsitem.title: USA: General Magic president resigns, CEO leaves.
newsitem.headline: General Magic president resigns, CEO leaves.

text.p: General Magic Inc., an Internet software producer, said Thursday that Marc Porat plans to step down as chief executive, and Robert Kelsch has resigned as president.
The Sunnyvale, Calif.-based company said the functions of president, CEO and chairman will be combined into a single position, which will be immediately filled by Steve Markman.
Markman had been executive vice president and general manager of the Novell products group for Novell Inc.
Porat, who founded General Magic in 1990, will become an adviser to the company and remain on the board.
Besides his work at Novell, Markman has held executive management positions with Hewlett-Packard Co. and First Pacific Networks Inc., General Magic said.
General Magic provides Internet software for business professionals, developers, device manufacturers, service providers and enterprises. It has offices in Columbia, S.C., Paris and Tokyo.
General Magic's stock rose 37.5 cents to $4.125 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.
